subject: Civil Engineering
title: Submarine Landslides
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Submarine Landslides.

hook.text: The 1929 Grand Banks earthquake triggered an underwater landslide — it snapped 12 cables.

buildup.text: Submarine slopes on continental shelves can be just as unstable as hillsides on land.

discovery.text: Underwater slides generate turbidity currents — fast-moving clouds of sediment and water.

twist.text: These flows can sever submarine cables and trigger tsunamis thousands of miles away.

climax.text: The Storegga Slide 8,000 years ago created a tsunami that hit Scotland and Norway.

punchline.text: The ocean floor can collapse just like a mountain — with bigger waves.

quiz.question: What dangerous phenomenon can submarine landslides trigger?
options: Volcanic eruptions on the ocean floor
Tsunamis that travel thousands of miles across the ocean
Permanent changes in ocean currents affecting climate

details.summary: Submarine landslides are massive movements of seafloor sediment triggered by earthquakes, rapid sedimentation, gas hydrate dissociation, or wave loading on continental slopes.
details.whyItMatters: Submarine landslides threaten offshore oil and gas platforms, subsea infrastructure, and coastal communities through tsunami generation. As offshore development expands into deeper water, this hazard grows increasingly important.
takeaways: Submarine slides can mobilize thousands of cubic kilometers of seafloor sediment
They generate tsunamis that affect coastlines hundreds of kilometers away
Gas hydrate dissociation in warming oceans may increase future slide frequency

faq.question: How large can submarine landslides be compared to terrestrial ones?
faq.answer: The Storegga Slide off Norway mobilized approximately 3,500 cubic kilometers of sediment, dwarfing any terrestrial landslide. These massive slides occur because continental slopes are very long, marine sediments are often weak and underconsolidated.

faq.question: How do submarine landslides generate tsunamis?
faq.answer: Submarine landslides rapidly displace the water column above them as they move. The displaced water forms tsunami waves that radiate outward. Unlike earthquake tsunamis that affect broad areas, landslide tsunamis can be locally extreme but dissipate faster with distance.
